kept.publisher: Roya News, quoting U.S. Central Command
kept.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) said its forces continue to enforce the naval blockade reimposed on Iran last month, as the US military expands maritime operations in the region. In its latest update, CENTCOM said that, as of Aug. 2, US forces have redirected 35 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two as part of the blockade.
kept.relevance: Provides a cutoff-day report of the authorized military command's statement that blockade enforcement was continuing.

kept.publisher: Reuters via MarketScreener; published August 1 and updated August 2, 2026
kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump has said the U.S. will hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a deal can be reached quickly to halt Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's official news agency IRNA reported on Sunday that negotiations between Tehran and Oman over the Strait of Hormuz were in their final stages, citing Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi.
kept.relevance: Documents a recent diplomatic opening while identifying Trump's announcement as a conditional pause in attacks rather than a declaration ending the naval blockade.

kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump said Sunday he decided to hold off on ordering American forces to carry out new strikes against Iran at the urging of Gulf allies Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. A regional official said the proposal announced by Trump over the weekend calls for the U.S. and Iran to return to negotiations and continue working out many of the issues that have stymied prior progress on the deal.
kept.relevance: Identifies the regional mediators and the prospective negotiating process that could provide a route to a broader agreement.

kept.publisher: Critical Threats Project / Institute for the Study of War
kept.excerpt: IRGC-affiliated Fars News denied on August 2 that Iran agreed to a plan to reopen the strait. An informed Iranian military source told Fars News that the strait will remain closed as long as the United States continues to conduct “hostile actions.” The source added that vessels can only transit through Iran's traffic separation scheme and with permission from the IRGC Navy.
kept.relevance: Shows contemporaneous Iranian resistance to the proposed shipping arrangement, a potential obstacle to an agreement involving general suspension of the U.S. blockade.

kept.excerpt: The White House on Friday signaled that President Donald Trump is weighing carrying out new strikes on Iran as the U.S. presses for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and abide by terms set out in a truce agreement the two sides forged last month only to quickly collapse.
kept.relevance: Establishes the coercive U.S. policy posture immediately before the cutoff weekend's diplomatic developments.

kept.excerpt: At the Commander in Chief's direction, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces will resume blockading maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on July 14 at 4 p.m. ET. CENTCOM forces will enforce the blockade against vessels transiting to or from Iranian ports and coastal areas. The U.S. military continues to support traffic flow through regional waters for all vessels not violating the blockade. The resumption of the U.S. blockade against Iran follows the initial implementation from April 13 to June 18.
kept.relevance: Defines the officially announced blockade's operational scope and supplies a dated precedent for an earlier blockade period ending.
